status: draft, not frozen; owner decisions Q-1 to Q-13 of 2026-10-17 applied
role: original logical acceptance descriptions for the E01 IFC export contract; not an exporter, IFC file or USD fixture

polarity.positive: the rule is satisfied or the described export succeeds as stated
polarity.negative: the rule fires: an element is exported with a listed loss, a warning is raised, or the request is refused with the listed code

rule_severity.error: the request is refused; the F04 code is stated
rule_severity.warning: reported, export continues; the F04 code is the one strict mode refuses with, if any
rule_severity.mapping: a mapping or format rule; breach is an exporter defect found by the acceptance cases, not a runtime diagnostic

id_scheme: Element ids are 019a7bf0-0000-7000-8000- followed by 12 digits: 300000 plus the number n of the element in the case.
Case ids are E01-POS-nn and E01-NEG-nn and never change once the contract is frozen.
comparison: Identifiers, strings, booleans, integers, codes, statuses and file bytes compare exactly.
Numbers follow CR-TOL-001 as in the F04 case file; dimensionless direction components use absolute 1e-6 at zero and relative 1e-6 otherwise.
assumptions: Cases describe logical inputs and outcomes. They are proposed future tests, not a runnable exporter, IFC file or USD fixture.

A case with a needs field depends on a limit being lifted, a harness hook, or one of the dependencies D1 (stored ProjectId) and D2 (Level concept) of section 19; it is not reachable with the stores of today.
Material and profile digests in cases stand for actual validated resources that the harness must supply; no placeholder hash is a real resource.
Quantity values are hand-derived from the box formulas of F06 section 8. Box meshes follow the F06 section 6 canonical order, which P01 is assumed to store in the derived layer.

rules.text: An element whose kind has no IFC mapping (every kind except plate, beam and column, reserved or unknown) is exported as IfcBuildingElementProxy and listed. It is never skipped, and it is not fatal in strict mode.

The export reads exactly one verified committed revision, the published head by default or an explicit RevisionId. A revision that cannot be read and verified completely is refused; there is no partial export.
IFC import, and any reading of IFC by BeamCraft, is outside this contract. A request to import is refused.
Export is read-only: it changes no authored state, derived state, revision or generation, and writes no attribute into the store.
An element whose lifecycle is deactivated is not exported and is listed (F10 section 3.2; owner decision Q-12). It is the only element that is not exported.
Every other element of the revision is exported. An element without usable geometry is exported without a representation and listed; nothing else is skipped.
contract_version is exactly 0.1.0 and the requested schema identifier is IFC4 (IFC4 ADD2 TC1), the only supported one.
The only output format is the clear-text STEP physical file. Any other requested format is refused.
No model view definition is claimed. The header names none and the file does not assert conformance to one.
The GlobalId of an element is E(ElementId) of section 3.1: alphabet, first character 0 to 3, big-endian bit order, 22 characters.

An ElementId that is not a canonical lowercase UUIDv7 with the RFC variant gets no GlobalId, with no repair, lowercasing, truncation, padding or hash fallback. In an export the element makes the request fail: a stored revision with such an id is not a valid revision.
The decoder accepts exactly 22 characters of the alphabet whose first character is 0, 1, 2 or 3. Everything else is rejected.

Entities that are not elements get a synthetic GlobalId from the SHA-256 construction of section 3.5, a function of the stored ProjectId, the LevelId or ElementId and the fixed role only (owner decision Q-11).
Two elements of the revision with the same ElementId refuse the export (F10 DV-BASE-002).
Two entities of one file with the same GlobalId, including a synthetic one equal to an element one, refuse the export.
The GlobalId is a pure function of the ElementId. It does not change with rename, edit, placement, revision, export run, platform or time; a copy has a new ElementId and so a new GlobalId.

The GlobalId is computed at export (and by the CLI helper) and is not persisted: no attribute is written to the authored or derived layer. A stored attribute of that name found in a layer is unknown content, preserved, ignored and never trusted (owner decision Q-6).
An explicit revision_id is a full canonical UUIDv7 text.
A required option is missing, an option is unknown or repeated, or a value is out of range. There is no project-id option: the ProjectId is read from the project entry.
An explicit revision_id names no committed revision of the store.
The project entry of the revision must record a ProjectId (dependency D1, section 19). A revision without one is refused; no ProjectId is invented or taken from an option.
The GlobalIds of the project, site, building, storeys and relationships derive from the stored ProjectId, so two exports of the same project agree and two projects never share them.
Each stored Level (dependency D2, section 19) becomes one IfcBuildingStorey with its name and elevation; the elements assigned to it are contained in it by one IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure.
An element assigned to a LevelId that no Level of the revision carries refuses the export.
An element with no level is contained in the IfcBuilding. A project with no Level has no storey.
A storey placement is the point (0, 0, elevation) relative to the building placement. Element placements stay relative to the building placement, so a level adds no arithmetic to any element number.

An element whose part-of record names an element that is not an exported IfcElementAssembly - no such element, or a kind without the assembly mapping - refuses the export: the aggregation would dangle.
The element placement becomes one IfcLocalPlacement relative to the building placement: Location is translation_mm, Axis is R(q) applied to (0,0,1), RefDirection is R(q) applied to (1,0,0).
A placement of a proxy element that cannot be read as a rigid pose (scale, shear, reflection, matrix form) is not exported: the element has no ObjectPlacement and no representation, and is listed.
A stored quaternion of a plate, beam or column outside the F04 section 3 caps refuses the export: the revision violates F04.
The quaternion is normalized before use; q and -q give identical output; negative zero is written as zero.
Every element with usable geometry has exactly one shape representation, identifier Body, type Tessellation, with exactly one IfcTriangulatedFaceSet item and nothing else (owner decision Q-2).

The face set is the published derived mesh of the pinned revision in its stored vertex and triangle order, in element-local coordinates, with 1-based indices; Closed is true for plate, beam and column and unset for any other kind. Normals are not written.
Mesh coordinates are the stored binary32 values written as the shortest decimal that parses back to the same binary32, unscaled millimetres (section 11.3).

An element that has no derived mesh (geometry status unsupported, for example a valid non-rectangular plate or a member with another profile kind), or whose mesh has a face that is not a triangle, is exported without a representation and listed. The code is the one strict mode refuses with.
For a plate, beam or column the stored derived mesh must equal the kernel's re-evaluation of the authored inputs (digest equality). A mismatch refuses the whole export.
A derived mesh that is structurally invalid (an index out of range, a non-finite coordinate, counts that disagree) refuses the export.
Holes are part of the mesh. No profile, extrusion, boolean, opening or void entity is written, and no authored parameter other than those in BeamCraft_Element and BeamCraft_Declared (section 9).
The volume of the exported face set, recomputed from the file by the divergence sum, equals the published volume within the bound of section 6.4.

Each distinct pinned material digest used by an exported element becomes one IfcMaterial, associated with all its elements by one IfcRelAssociatesMaterial. An element without a material gets no association and no invented default.

IfcMaterial.Name is the declared grade, otherwise the text Unspecified. Description is the declared standard when present. The full digest is always written as the property MaterialDigest of the property group BeamCraft_Material (owner decision Q-9).
MassDensity is written only when the definition authors a density, as received. An unknown density is never written as zero or any default.
A pinned profile or material digest of an exported element that does not resolve to a definition refuses the export (F10 DV-BASE-006).
A quantity is written only from a stored record whose signature equals the freshly computed one and whose status is current. Nothing is recomputed at export time.

A quantity whose freshness is stale, missing, unknown or unsupported is not written (no zero, no previous value); its status is written in BeamCraft_Element and the omission is listed (owner decision Q-5).
Mapping of the published quantities: volume to NetVolume, mass to NetWeight, in the IFC4 base quantity set of the product type and in SI units (section 8.2).
GrossVolume and GrossWeight are written, with the same values, only for an element without operations (a plate without holes, every member). Otherwise they are omitted.
A stored record with status current whose value is not finite, or whose volume is not greater than zero, refuses the export.
BeamCraft_Element names the statuses, signatures and algorithm label of the records, so a reader can compare them with the derived layer.

The IFC4 plate base quantity set has no weight quantities. A plate's current mass is written as the properties NetWeightKg and GrossWeightKg of BeamCraft_Element (IfcMassMeasure, kilograms), under the same freshness and Gross rules.

Declared section values of a member's profile definition (designation, standard, area, mass per metre, surface per metre) are written, when present, in the separate property set BeamCraft_Declared, never in a quantity set (owner decision Q-10).

Declared values are written as authored, without conversion or check, in properties whose names carry the unit (DeclaredSectionAreaMm2, DeclaredMassPerMeterKg, DeclaredSurfacePerMeterM2), each with a description that says it is declared and not computed.
Each exported element has one property set BeamCraft_Element with the properties of section 9.1.
A BeamCraft property set or group name never starts with Pset_ or Qto_, except Pset_MaterialCommon and the Qto_ sets of the specification used as section 8 and 7 state.
No property, string or header field contains an actor id, credential, private path, host name, user name or wall-clock time.

A BeamCraft string written into an IfcLabel attribute (IfcRoot.Name of an element, storey or project, IfcObject.ObjectType, IfcMaterial.Name) is limited to 255 characters. A longer text is truncated to 255 code points and the truncation is listed; the full text is kept in an unbounded IfcText: the property Label (element), FullName in BeamCraft_Material (material), IfcRoot.Description (storey, project) or ElementKind in BeamCraft_Element (proxy ObjectType). Other BeamCraft strings are written as IfcText, so no length limit applies to them.
The unit assignment is: length milli metre, plane angle radian, area square metre, volume cubic metre, mass kilogram, mass density kilogram per cubic metre (derived unit).
Lengths and coordinates are written exactly as the internal millimetre values (mesh values as their binary32 text). No scaling is applied to any length; the storey elevation is written as stored.
Elements, levels and relationship members are processed and listed in ascending canonical id order (byte comparison of the 36-character lowercase text); materials in ascending digest order.
STEP instance numbers are assigned by a counter in the fixed emission order of section 11.2.
A binary64 REAL and a binary32 REAL are each written as the shortest decimal text that parses back to the same value of its own type, in the notation of section 11.3.
Strings are escaped as in section 11.4. The whole file is 7-bit ASCII with LF line ends.
Header fields are the fixed values of section 11.5; the only variable one is the time stamp derived from the RevisionId (owner decision Q-4).
The same revision, options and exporter version give a byte-identical file and report. No clock, random source, locale, thread count, hash-map order, environment variable or path influences them.
Cross-platform byte identity is claimed only when no member has a nonzero roll; with a nonzero roll it depends on the unresolved sin/cos reproducibility question (F06 section 2).
The export result uses the F10 section 6.3 envelope precedence: an unavailable input makes the status incomplete and the primary code DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE, before any other error.
A failing output sink or file system gives no output file. The file is written to a temporary name and installed only after complete success.
An existing output file is not replaced unless overwrite is requested; a symbolic link or reparse point at the output name or its parent is refused.
Cancellation before the install point discards all work and leaves no file.

In strict mode only an element-level finding that carries an F04 code (IFC_GEOMETRY_ABSENT and IFC_PLACEMENT_ABSENT, code UNSUPPORTED_GEOMETRY) refuses the export, with the code of the first such finding in finding order (F10 section 6.4). Warnings and info without a code (proxies, quantity omissions, truncated names, deactivated elements) are never fatal.

An optional entity is written only when it has content, so no mandatory attribute or relationship is empty: IfcElementQuantity and its IfcRelDefinesByProperties only with at least one quantity; BeamCraft_Declared and its relationship only with a declared value; Pset_MaterialCommon only with a density; IfcMaterial and its IfcRelAssociatesMaterial only with at least one exported element using it; IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure (of a storey or of the building) only with at least one exported element; the building-to-storeys IfcRelAggregates only with at least one storey; a representation only with a mesh.
At most 65,536 elements are exported in one file; more refuse the export before any output is produced.
The output is at most 268,435,456 bytes. The writer checks the running size before each write; exceeding it refuses the export and removes the temporary file.
Every count in the writer is bounded by a cap enforced upstream or by LIM-001, 002 and 005; no allocation is sized by an unchecked input, no recursion is used and no input-derived index is used.
The report keeps at most 256 findings in the F10 order and states total_findings and truncated; the per-element table is complete.
A single mesh of more than 262,144 vertices or 524,288 triangles, or a project of more than 1,024 levels, refuses the export.

Acceptance of E02 includes validating a written file with the owner's chosen independent tool, Altiro Desktop (owner decision Q-8), run locally as a separate process with no upload of the file; its admission is an open E02 gate (section 17).
Every export is an engine API call first; the CLI command adds no computation and no private path (AGENTS.md section 3).
The export report of section 15.4 is deterministic, lists every element's GlobalId, representation, quantity freshness and omissions, and carries the SHA-256 of the file.

cases.derivation: Bytes 01 9a 7b f0 00 00 70 00 80 00 00 00 00 20 00 01. The first character is the top two bits (00) = 0. The remaining 126 bits in groups of six give the indices 1, 38, 39, 47, 48, 0, 0, 1, 48, 0, 8, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 8, 0, 0, 1, which are the characters 1 c d l m 0 0 1 m 0 8 0 0 0 0 0 0 8 0 0 1.
